docs.text: The Great Lakes Waterway — a system which permits vessels to travel all the way from the Atlantic Ocean to Duluth, Minnesota, an astonishing 2,340 miles into the continental interior — is not just an audacious civil engineering project, but also a feat of sophisticated shared US/Canadian governance.

Oh it is. It's designed to maximize capacity on the Great Lakes while still fitting through the Soo Locks to get taconite pellets from the Mesabi Range in Minnesota/Wisconsin to the steel mills of Detroit/Toledo/Cleveland/Buffalo. They're basically massive barges.

#OnThisDay June 26, 1959 President Eisenhower and Queen Elizabeth II dedicate the St Lawrence Seaway aboard the royal yacht "Britannia" at Montréal, opening the Great Lakes to large transatlantic vessels for the first time. Duluth Minnesota becomes the farthest inland seaport in the World.

Fun fact: The twin seaports of Duluth, MN and Superior, WI serve ocean ships over 2,300 miles from the ocean. They rely on the Great Lakes and Canada’s St. Lawrence Seaway to do so.

TBF, Did you know that Lake Superior is connected to the Atlantic Ocean by the St. Lawrence Seaway? The 2,343 mile (3,770 kilometer) trip takes about seven days by boat from Duluth/Superior, the busiest inland port in the country, with more than 1,000 vessels visiting each year.
